storyDescription: Yield forecast begins uncertain in May, improves rapidly through strong June vegetative growth, experiences a slight plateau during a July dry spell and heat wave, then stabilizes at 184.3 bu/ac (+4.7% vs baseline) with 87% confidence as August rain recovers.

snapshots.stageSubtext: VE / V2 - Stand establishment & initial seedling emergence

explanations.title: Adequate seedbed moisture at emergence
explanations.description: Spring rainfall provided sufficient topsoil moisture for uniform stand establishment across all plot sectors.

explanations.title: High seasonal uncertainty band
explanations.description: Early-stage forecasting relies heavily on historical climatology and seedling density proxies, leaving wide prediction intervals.

snapshots.stageSubtext: V6 / V8 - Rapid stem elongation & whorl development

explanations.title: Strong canopy closure and chlorophyll accumulation
explanations.description: Vegetation indices (NDRE slope +0.14/wk) indicate vigorous leaf expansion during early rapid vegetative growth.

explanations.title: Balanced thermal time accumulation
explanations.description: Thermal units tracked 6% above the 10-year mean, promoting steady nodal root establishment.

snapshots.stageSubtext: V12 / V14 - Rapid biomass surge approaching tassel formation

explanations.title: Above-average biomass index prior to flowering
explanations.description: Canopy NDVI crossed 0.74 two calendar days ahead of the regional 5-year average curve.

explanations.title: Subtle moisture draw in topsoil layer
explanations.description: Precipitation trailed normal by 14%, but deep soil water holding capacity cushioned crop transpiration demand.

snapshots.stageSubtext: VT / R1 - Tasseling & silking; peak moisture sensitivity

explanations.title: Strong canopy vigor preceding pollination window
explanations.description: Vegetation indices remained consistently above historical field baseline during pre-tasseling biomass accumulation.

explanations.title: Developing dry spell during critical flowering
explanations.description: Precipitation was 26% below normal, introducing atmospheric water stress during pollen shed.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R2 - Blister stage; kernel set established under high evaporative demand

explanations.title: Strong mid-season canopy development
explanations.description: Vegetation indices remained above the historical field baseline during a key mid-season period, establishing high kernel sink capacity.

explanations.title: Below-normal rainfall during pollination
explanations.description: Rainfall during the previous 30 days was approximately 31% below the long-term baseline, tempering top-end yield upside.

explanations.title: Moderate available water capacity
explanations.description: Soil characteristics may partially buffer short periods of rainfall deficit by supplying deep root moisture reserves.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R3 - Milk stage; kernel starch accumulation begins

explanations.title: Canopy greenness resilience through milk stage
explanations.description: NDRE reflectance signals sustained upper-canopy nitrogen status despite elevated evaporative stress.

explanations.title: Dry spell duration extended to 14 days
explanations.description: Topsoil moisture depleted; yield forecast plateaued as transpiration restrictions bounded further gains.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R4 / R5 - Dough to early dent; late summer rainfall replenished soil reserves

explanations.title: Rainfall recovery averted late kernel abortion
explanations.description: Late July / early August rain events replenished subsoil reserves during critical grain dry matter deposition.

explanations.title: Tightening forecast variance band
explanations.description: Over 80% of seasonal biological yield potential has been fixed by kernel count and initial ear fill rate.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R6 - Physiological maturity (black layer formed); harvest yield locked

explanations.title: Physiological maturity completed with above-normal test weight
explanations.description: Black layer formation observed across field survey with full kernel dent and minimal ear rot.

explanations.title: Seasonal yield established +5.2% over regional baseline
explanations.description: Final yield forecast locked at 185.1 bu/ac with 95% confidence interval narrowing to ±5.6 bu/ac.

events.title: Heavy rainfall event
events.hoverDetail: Heavy rainfall: 38 mm precipitation recharged soil water profile with zero pooling damage.

events.title: Dry spell begins
events.hoverDetail: Dry spell begins: Extended zero-precipitation window coincided with early tassel initiation.

events.title: High heat period
events.hoverDetail: High-temperature exposure: 4 days above 95°F during previous 10 days elevated vapor pressure deficit.

events.title: Rainfall recovery
events.hoverDetail: Rainfall recovery: 29 mm broken weather front ended moisture deficit, securing grain fill.

storyDescription: Severe prolonged moisture deficit throughout June and July on coarse glacial ridge soil caused canopy stunted growth and leaf curling, dragging predicted yield down to 154.2 bu/ac (-12.4% vs regional baseline).

snapshots.stageSubtext: VE / V2 - Stand emergence on sandy-clay knoll

explanations.title: Fair early emergence on ridge topography
explanations.description: Initial emergence was uniform, though sandier knolls drained rapidly.

snapshots.stageSubtext: V6 - Growth slowdown on lower water holding areas

explanations.title: Topsoil moisture depletion during whorl growth
explanations.description: Rainfall lagged 38% behind regional normals, inducing early stomatal closure.

snapshots.stageSubtext: V10 / V12 - Canopy depression detectable from orbit

explanations.title: Canopy NDRE dropped 18% below field history
explanations.description: Vegetation indices plateaued early as lower leaves showed drought fired margins.

snapshots.stageSubtext: VT - Silking delayed by drought stress

explanations.title: Anthesis-silking interval (ASI) elongation
explanations.description: Prolonged dry spell delayed silk emergence relative to pollen shed, reducing ovule fertilization.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R2 - Blister stage with significant kernel tip dieback

explanations.title: Acute 30-day precipitation deficit (-58%)
explanations.description: Rainfall total of 24 mm over the past 30 days is the lowest recorded for this plot in 12 years.

explanations.title: Low available water capacity in subsoil
explanations.description: Sandy loam profile with only 85 cm rooting depth failed to retain buffer moisture against heat spikes.

explanations.title: Vegetation indices significantly below regional benchmark
explanations.description: NDVI of 0.67 is 14% beneath county median, signaling reduced active photosynthetic surface.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R3 - Kernel abortion fixed

explanations.title: Ear kernel abortion completed at ear tips
explanations.description: Model considered physiological sink reduction permanent, limiting maximum ear mass.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R4 - Modest late rain too late to restore ear size

explanations.title: Late rain supported test weight but ear count locked
explanations.description: Early August shower stabilized remaining kernels without restoring lost tip seeds.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R6 - Early premature black layer

explanations.title: Premature black layer triggered 6 days early
explanations.description: Drought-induced canopy death forced premature physiological maturity.

events.title: Prolonged dry streak begins
events.hoverDetail: Dry streak begins: Coarse sandy ridge depleted top 20cm available water.

events.title: Severe canopy moisture deficit
events.hoverDetail: Severe moisture deficit: Mid-day leaf rolling observed consistently across all zones.

events.title: Excessive heat spike
events.hoverDetail: Heat spike: Peak daytime temperatures exceeded 97°F during critical pollination.

storyDescription: Textbook benchmark season with rainfall tracking close to historical means, moderate thermal accumulation, and steady canopy progression tracking the regional baseline yield closely at 189.5 bu/ac (+0.8%).

snapshots.stageSubtext: V2 - Uniform emergence on flat prairie soil

explanations.title: Prime organic matter and deep soil profile
explanations.description: Drummer silty clay loam with 4.2% OM provides excellent initial nutrient and moisture buffers.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R2 - Blister stage with normal ear development

explanations.title: Steady rainfall aligned with historical normal
explanations.description: 62 mm past 30 days stayed within 3% of normal, maintaining optimal soil moisture tensiometer levels.

explanations.title: Moderate heat load during pollination
explanations.description: Only 1 day exceeded 95°F, avoiding significant pollen desiccation during peak tassel shedding.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R6 - Full maturity, standard yield achieved

explanations.title: Final yield matched 5-year average with low spatial variance
explanations.description: Uniform topography and reliable tile drainage yielded steady production across all 120 acres.

events.title: Timely seasonal rainfall
events.hoverDetail: Timely rain event provided ideal soil moisture at V8 initiation.

events.title: Mild heat front
events.hoverDetail: Brief single-day temperature crest well handled by deep silty clay loam reserves.

storyDescription: Extreme heat wave during the July pollination window (9 days > 95°F with peak 101°F) drove intense atmospheric vapor pressure deficit, causing silk desiccation and poor kernel set despite pivot irrigation, reducing yield to 162.4 bu/ac (-8.8%).

snapshots.stageSubtext: V2 - Center pivot emergence in loess soil

explanations.title: Pivot-assisted early emergence
explanations.description: Center pivot irrigation ensured uniform stand density across high-plains loess.

snapshots.stageSubtext: VT / R1 - Severe heat wave during pollination

explanations.title: Extreme heat exposure (9 days > 95°F)
explanations.description: Temperatures surpassed 95°F for 9 consecutive pollination days, degrading pollen viability despite irrigation.

explanations.title: Elevated atmospheric vapor pressure deficit (VPD)
explanations.description: Extreme evaporative demand exceeded canopy uptake rate, causing silk drying prior to ovule fertilization.

explanations.title: Deep loess soil water buffering
explanations.description: Subsoil Holdrege loess prevented catastrophic leaf firing but could not prevent reproductive heat damage.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R6 - Reduced kernel count per ear established

explanations.title: Final ear inspections confirm reduced kernel rows
explanations.description: Thermal damage during VT fixed kernel numbers approximately 14% below regional target.

events.title: Heat wave begins
events.hoverDetail: Heat wave begins: Persistent high-pressure dome trapped extreme temperatures across Central Platte.

events.title: Peak thermal record
events.hoverDetail: Peak thermal exposure: Afternoon air temp reached 101°F with relative humidity under 24%.

storyDescription: Spectacular early season with peak vegetative NDVI surging yield projections up to 198 bu/ac in late June, followed by persistent late August torrential storms and ponding that induced root anoxia and tar spot lesions, tapering final forecast to 174.5 bu/ac (-9.1%).

snapshots.stageSubtext: V2 - Rapid germination on warm black soils

explanations.title: Prime Des Moines Lobe fertility
explanations.description: High 4.8% organic matter supplied optimal early nitrogen mineralization.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R2 - Dense canopy holding peak projections before late storms

explanations.title: Exceptional mid-season biomass and greenness index
explanations.description: NDVI reached 0.88 with unbroken canopy cover across 95% of field acreage.

explanations.title: Abundant moisture in top 100 cm profile
explanations.description: Rainfall 24% above normal supported high kernel counts and expansive ear length.

snapshots.stageSubtext: R5 / R6 - Late waterlogging and disease depression revealed

explanations.title: Excess late precipitation causing root zone hypoxia
explanations.description: 164 mm rain in late August saturated prairie potholes, suffocating lower nodal roots.

explanations.title: Fungal tar spot lesions accelerated leaf senescence
explanations.description: High relative humidity promoted late foliar pathogen outbreak, clipping test weight.

events.title: Peak vegetative surge
events.hoverDetail: Peak vegetative surge: Optimum soil moisture created exceptionally dense canopy architecture.

events.title: Torrential storm & standing water
events.hoverDetail: Torrential downpour caused ponding across central field depression with root hypoxia.
